steps.title: Create the fake data store
steps.body:
Agents are only as good as the systems behind them. Start with a small JSON file of orders, shipments and policies. The customers are clearly fake.

One order has a tracking number, one is still processing (no tracking), one is delivered. That spread lets you test different tool paths.

steps.title: Define the tools, schemas and validation
steps.body:
TOOLS is exactly what the Messages API expects: a name, a description the model reads to decide when to call it, and a JSON schema for the input. Good descriptions matter as much as good code.

Never trust tool arguments. The model can send a missing field, a wrong type or an injected string. validate() checks required keys, extra keys, types and id formats before any data is touched. execute_tool() never raises: errors come back as text with is_error=True so the model can recover (for example, ask the user for the right order id). Create an empty agent/__init__.py too so agent is a package.

steps.title: Write two model clients: real and fake
steps.body:
RealLLM wraps client.messages.create with the model from MODEL. FakeLLM returns objects with the same shape (stop_reason plus content blocks with type tool_use or text), decided by simple rules: look up the order, then track it if the user asks where it is, then search policy for return or refund words, then answer.

Because both expose the same create() method, the loop cannot tell them apart. That is what lets tests run offline and for free.

steps.title: Write the agent loop with a cap and a trace
steps.body:
The loop: call the model; if stop_reason is tool_use, run every requested tool and send all results back in ONE user message; repeat. Stop on end_turn, on any other stop reason (max_tokens, refusal), or when max_iterations is reached.

The assistant turn is appended exactly as returned, so tool_use (and any thinking) blocks stay intact. Every step goes to a Trace, one JSON line per event, which is what you read when a customer says the bot gave a wrong answer.

steps.title: Add a command line entry point
steps.body: main.py prints each tool call and the final answer and appends the trace to trace.jsonl. The mode (fake or real) comes from LLM_MODE.
steps.code:
"""Command line entry point: python main.py "Where is my order A1001?" """
import os
import sys

from agent.llm import make_llm
from agent.loop import Trace, run_agent


def main():
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "Where is my order A1001?"
    trace = Trace(os.environ.get("TRACE_FILE", "trace.jsonl"))
    result = run_agent(question, make_llm(), trace=trace)
    for event in result["trace"]:
        if event["kind"] == "tool":
            flag = " (error)" if event["is_error"] else ""
            print(f"  [step {event['step']}] {event['name']}({event['input']}){flag}")
    print(f"\nAnswer: {result['answer']}")
    print(f"Steps: {result['steps']}  |  trace appended to {trace.path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json

import pytest

from agent.tools import ToolError, execute_tool, load_store, validate


@pytest.fixture
def store():
    return load_store()


def test_get_order_found(store):
    out, is_error = execute_tool(store, "get_order", {"order_id": "A1001"})
    assert not is_error
    assert json.loads(out)["tracking"] == "TRK-555001"


def test_get_order_missing_is_error_not_crash(store):
    out, is_error = execute_tool(store, "get_order", {"order_id": "A9999"})
    assert is_error and "no order" in out


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "name,args",
    [
        ("get_order", {}),                                  # missing argument
        ("get_order", {"order_id": "1001; DROP TABLE"}),    # bad format
        ("get_order", {"order_id": "A1001", "admin": "1"}),  # unexpected argument
        ("track_shipment", {"tracking_number": 42}),        # wrong type
        ("delete_order", {"order_id": "A1001"}),            # unknown tool
    ],
)
def test_validation_rejects_bad_args(name, args):
    with pytest.raises(ToolError):
        validate(name, args)


def test_search_policy_ranks_returns_first(store):
    out, _ = execute_tool(store, "search_policy", {"query": "how do I return and get a refund"})
    assert json.loads(out)["results"][0]["id"] == "returns"

steps.title: Test the agent loop, including a runaway model
steps.body: LoopingLLM is a deliberately broken model that asks for a tool forever. The test proves the iteration cap stops it and hands off to a human. Other tests check tool order for a tracking question, the policy path, a missing order, and that the trace file is written.
steps.code:
from types import SimpleNamespace

from agent.llm import FakeLLM
from agent.loop import Trace, run_agent


def tool_names(result):
    return [e["name"] for e in result["trace"] if e["kind"] == "tool"]


def test_tracking_question_chains_two_tools():
    result = run_agent("Where is my order A1001?", FakeLLM())
    assert tool_names(result) == ["get_order", "track_shipment"]
    assert "in transit" in result["answer"] and result["steps"] == 3


def test_policy_question_uses_search():
    result = run_agent("Can I return something I bought?", FakeLLM())
    assert tool_names(result) == ["search_policy"]
    assert "30 days" in result["answer"]


def test_unknown_order_is_reported_gracefully():
    result = run_agent("Where is order A9999?", FakeLLM())
    assert any(e["kind"] == "tool" and e["is_error"] for e in result["trace"])
    assert "could not find" in result["answer"]


class LoopingLLM:
    """A misbehaving model that asks for a tool forever."""

    def create(self, system, messages, tools):
        block = SimpleNamespace(type="tool_use", id=f"t{len(messages)}", name="get_order", input={"order_id": "A1001"})
        return SimpleNamespace(stop_reason="tool_use", content=[block])


def test_iteration_cap_stops_runaway_loop():
    result = run_agent("loop please", LoopingLLM(), max_iterations=3)
    assert result["steps"] == 3
    assert result["trace"][-1]["kind"] == "capped"
    assert "human agent" in result["answer"]


def test_trace_written_to_file(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "trace.jsonl"
    run_agent("Where is my order A1001?", FakeLLM(), trace=Trace(path))
    lines = path.read_text().strip().splitlines()
    assert len(lines) >= 5  # user, model, tool, model, tool, model, final

project.interview: I built an order-support agent with a hand-written tool loop on the Anthropic Messages API: three narrow tools, schema plus format validation on every argument, errors returned to the model as is_error results instead of exceptions, an iteration cap with a human handoff, and a JSONL trace per step. A fake model with the same interface made the loop testable offline, including a runaway-model test. The trade-offs I would mention are narrow tools versus one generic query tool (safer and easier to evaluate, but more tools to maintain), and the SDK tool runner versus a manual loop (less code versus full control over caps and tracing).

ideas: An agent is a loop: model asks for a tool, your code runs it, results go back, repeat until end_turn.
Tool descriptions and schemas are prompts; the model chooses tools by reading them.
Validate every tool argument and return errors as is_error results so the model can recover.
A fake model with the same interface makes agent logic testable offline and deterministic.
traps: No iteration cap: a confused model can call tools forever and burn money.
Sending tool results back in separate user messages, or dropping the assistant turn that contained the tool_use blocks, which breaks the conversation shape.
Hard-coding a model id or API key in code instead of reading them from the environment.
qa: Why return tool errors to the model instead of raising?

Because the model can often fix the problem itself: ask the user for a valid order id, or try a different tool. Raising ends the whole conversation. Returning a clear error with is_error=True keeps the loop alive, and the trace still records the failure for debugging.
How would you stop an agent from doing something harmful with a tool?

Keep tools narrow (get_order, not run_sql), validate arguments against strict formats, enforce permissions in the tool code not the prompt, cap iterations, require human confirmation for writes like cancel or refund, and log every call so you can audit it.

steps.title: Write the mock CRM as plain Python
steps.body:
Keep business logic separate from the protocol. crm_data.py has four fake companies, some notes, and four functions: search, get, add_note and pipeline_summary. No MCP here, so it is trivial to test.

Errors are helpful on purpose: an unknown id tells the model to call search_customers first. Error text is guidance for the model.

steps.title: Wrap it in a FastMCP server
steps.body:
@mcp.tool() turns a function into an MCP tool. The function name becomes the tool name, type hints become the input schema, and the docstring becomes the description the model reads. @mcp.resource() exposes read-only data at a URI; the client decides when to load it.

The critical detail for stdio servers: stdout is the protocol channel. A stray print() corrupts messages, so logging goes to stderr. mcp.run() uses stdio by default.

steps.title: Write a tiny MCP client to smoke-test it
steps.body: smoke_client.py starts the server as a subprocess over stdio, exactly like Claude Desktop does, then initializes a session, lists tools and resources, calls a tool and reads the resource. If this works, a real client will work.
steps.code:
"""Start the server as a subprocess and talk MCP to it, like Claude Desktop would."""
import asyncio
import sys

from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client


async def main():
    params = StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=["crm_server.py"])
    async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            tools = await session.list_tools()
            print("tools:", [t.name for t in tools.tools])
            resources = await session.list_resources()
            print("resources:", [str(r.uri) for r in resources.resources])
            result = await session.call_tool("search_customers", {"query": "trial"})
            print("search_customers(trial):", result.content[0].text)
            summary = await session.read_resource("crm://pipeline/summary")
            print(summary.contents[0].text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

steps.title: Unit-test the tool functions directly
steps.body: In FastMCP 1.x the decorators return your original function, so tests call search_customers() and friends like normal Python. A fixture resets the notes so tests do not leak state. The last test asks the server itself to list its tools and resources, catching registration mistakes.

import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
import crm_data  # noqa: E402
import crm_server  # noqa: E402


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def fresh_data():

def test_search_by_name_and_stage():
    assert [c["id"] for c in crm_server.search_customers("acme")] == ["C001"]
    assert [c["id"] for c in crm_server.search_customers("trial")] == ["C002"]


def test_search_limit_is_clamped():
    assert len(crm_server.search_customers("", limit=1000)) <= 20


def test_get_customer_includes_notes():
    record = crm_server.get_customer("C003")
    assert record["stage"] == "negotiation"
    assert "SSO" in record["notes"][0]


def test_unknown_customer_raises_helpful_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="search_customers"):
        crm_server.get_customer("C999")


def test_add_note_appends_and_validates():
    out = crm_server.add_note("C002", "  Trial extended by 2 weeks. ")
    assert out["notes"][-1].endswith("Trial extended by 2 weeks.")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        crm_server.add_note("C002", "x" * 501)


def test_resource_text():
    text = crm_server.pipeline_summary()
    assert "negotiation: 1" in text and "Total ARR: $165,000" in text


def test_server_registers_tools_and_resource():
    tools = asyncio.run(crm_server.mcp.list_tools())
    assert {t.name for t in tools} == {"search_customers", "get_customer", "add_note"}
    resources = asyncio.run(crm_server.mcp.list_resources())
    assert [str(r.uri) for r in resources] == ["crm://pipeline/summary"]

project.interview: I built an MCP server that exposes a mock CRM to any MCP client: three tools (search, get, add note) and a read-only pipeline resource, using FastMCP so type hints and docstrings become the schema. I kept business logic in plain Python so it is unit-tested directly, then verified the protocol with MCP Inspector and a small stdio client before wiring it into Claude Desktop. Trade-offs I would raise: stdio is simple and local but single-user, while HTTP needs real auth; and write tools like add_note need confirmation and audit logging because the model, not a human, decides when to call them.

ideas: MCP separates tools (actions the model may call) from resources (data the client may load).
Write the integration once as an MCP server and every MCP client can use it.
In FastMCP, type hints and docstrings become the tool schema and description, so write them for the model.
Keep business logic out of the protocol layer so it can be unit-tested directly.
traps: Printing to stdout in a stdio server, which corrupts the protocol stream. Log to stderr.
Relative paths or the system python in claude_desktop_config.json; Claude Desktop needs absolute paths to the venv's interpreter.
Installing mcp 2.x and copying 1.x FastMCP examples; the import moved, so pin the version or port the code.
qa: When would you expose something as a resource instead of a tool?

A resource is read-only context the client or user chooses to load, like a pipeline summary or a schema. A tool is something the model decides to call, possibly with side effects. If it changes data or needs arguments the model chooses, make it a tool; if it is reference data, a resource is simpler and safer.
How would you make this MCP server safe to give to a customer's sales team?

Run it over HTTP with real authentication, enforce per-user permissions inside each tool, keep write tools narrow with validation and confirmation, log every call with the user identity, rate-limit, and never return fields the caller is not allowed to see.

steps.title: Add the documents with ACL front matter
steps.body: Ten short, generated policy documents. Each starts with a title and an acl: all (everyone), hr, or finance. The ACL travels with every chunk so retrieval can filter on it.
steps.code:
# ===== docs/budget_approval.md =====
---
title: Budget approval (finance)
acl: finance
---
Purchases under 1,000 dollars need approval from your manager only. Purchases from 1,000 to 10,000 dollars need approval from the department head.

Any purchase over 10,000 dollars requires approval from the CFO before a purchase order is issued.

Budgets are set each November for the following fiscal year, which starts on February 1.

# ===== docs/expenses.md =====
---
title: Expense reimbursement
acl: all
---
Submit expense reports within 30 days of the purchase date using the expense tool. Reports submitted later than 90 days are not reimbursed.

An itemized receipt is required for every expense over 25 dollars. Alcohol and personal entertainment are never reimbursable.

Reimbursements are paid with the next payroll run after your manager approves the report.

# ===== docs/parental_leave.md =====
---
title: Parental leave
acl: all
---
Primary caregivers receive 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave. Secondary caregivers receive 8 weeks of fully paid leave.

Parental leave can be taken any time within 12 months of the birth, adoption or foster placement of a child.

Tell HR at least 30 days before your planned leave start date when possible, so your team can plan coverage.

# ===== docs/performance_reviews.md =====
---
title: Performance reviews (HR internal)
acl: hr
---
Performance reviews happen twice a year, in April and October. Managers rate each employee on a scale from 1 to 5.

An employee rated 1 or 2 in two consecutive reviews is placed on a 60-day performance improvement plan (PIP).

HR calibrates ratings across teams before results are shared with employees.

# ===== docs/pto.md =====
---
title: Paid time off
acl: all
---

steps.title: Write the embedders
steps.body:
HashingEmbedder is the offline mode: it hashes each word and word pair into one of 1024 buckets and normalizes the vector. It is deterministic and instant, but purely lexical: it does not know that vacation means PTO.

SentenceTransformerEmbedder is the real mode (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by default, 384 dimensions). Both return unit vectors, so a dot product is cosine similarity. EMBED_MODE picks one.

steps.title: Ingest, chunk, store and retrieve with an ACL filter
steps.body:
load_docs parses the front matter. chunk_doc splits on blank lines and packs paragraphs into chunks up to 400 characters, with ids like pto#1 that citations will use. Each chunk is embedded with its title prefixed so it keeps context.

InMemoryStore is the fallback for pgvector: a numpy matrix plus metadata. The key line sets forbidden chunks' scores to minus infinity BEFORE ranking, so restricted text can never be retrieved, let alone sent to a model. Create an empty rag/__init__.py too.

steps.title: Answer with citations, or abstain
steps.body:
If nothing relevant is retrieved (top score under MIN_SCORE) the system says it does not know instead of guessing. In fake mode the answer is the sentence from the top chunk that best overlaps the question, followed by its chunk id. In real mode Claude gets the chunks inside source tags and must cite a source id after every sentence.

MIN_SCORE is tuned for the hashing embedder; re-tune it when you switch embedders.
steps.code:
"""Answer a question from retrieved chunks, with [chunk-id] citations."""
import os
import re

from rag.embed import tokens
from rag.index import retrieve

NO_ANSWER = "I don't know based on the documents you can access."
MIN_SCORE = 0.08  # below this, retrieval found nothing relevant: abstain instead of guessing

SYSTEM = (
    "Answer the employee's question using ONLY the sources provided. After each sentence, "
    "cite the source id in square brackets, like [pto#0]. If the sources do not contain the "
    f"answer, reply exactly: {NO_ANSWER}"
)


def sentences(text):
    return [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?\]])\s+(?!\[)", text) if s.strip()]


def fake_answer(question, hits):
    """Offline mode: return the sentence from the top chunk that best overlaps the question."""
    top = hits[0][0]
    q = set(tokens(question))
    best = max(sentences(top.text), key=lambda s: len(q & set(tokens(s))))
    return f"{best} [{top.id}]"


def real_answer(question, hits):
    import anthropic

    context = "\n\n".join(f"<source id=\"{c.id}\" title=\"{c.title}\">\n{c.text}\n</source>" for c, _ in hits)
    response = anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create(
        model=os.environ["MODEL"],
        max_tokens=16000,
        system=SYSTEM,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"}],
    )
    return "".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text").strip()


def answer(question, store, embedder, groups=(), k=3):
    hits = retrieve(store, embedder, question, groups, k)
    if not hits or hits[0][1] < MIN_SCORE:
        return {"answer": NO_ANSWER, "hits": hits}
    mode = os.environ.get("LLM_MODE", "fake")
    text = real_answer(question, hits) if mode == "real" else fake_answer(question, hits)
    return {"answer": text, "hits": hits}

steps.title: Add a CLI to ask one question
steps.body: ask.py shows the retrieved chunks with scores and ACLs, then the answer. --groups sets which ACL groups the user belongs to.
steps.code:
"""Ask one question: python ask.py "How many PTO days do I get?" --groups hr"""
import argparse

from rag.answer import answer
from rag.embed import make_embedder
from rag.index import build_index

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("question")
parser.add_argument("--groups", nargs="*", default=[], help="ACL groups the user belongs to, e.g. hr finance")
parser.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=3)
args = parser.parse_args()

embedder = make_embedder()
store = build_index(embedder)
result = answer(args.question, store, embedder, args.groups, args.k)
print("Retrieved:")
for chunk, score in result["hits"]:
    print(f"  {score:.3f}  {chunk.id:<22} ({chunk.acl})")
print(f"\nAnswer: {result['answer']}")

steps.title: Write the golden set
steps.body: 15 questions, each with the user's groups, the document that should be retrieved, and a key fact the answer must contain. q15 is an ACL test: a regular user asks about HR-only salary bands, and the HR document must never appear in the results.

steps.title: Write the eval script and quality gates
steps.body:
recall@k: did the expected document appear in the top k? fact_accuracy: does the answer contain the key fact? faithfulness: for each answer sentence, does it cite a retrieved chunk and do at least 70 percent of its content words appear in that chunk? It is a cheap proxy; LLM-as-judge is the usual upgrade. acl_leaks counts forbidden documents retrieved.

The script exits with code 1 when a gate fails, so the same command works in CI.
steps.code:
"""Run the golden set: retrieval recall@k, fact accuracy, faithfulness, ACL leaks.

Usage: python eval.py [--k 3]      Exit code 1 if a quality gate fails (use it in CI).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from rag.answer import NO_ANSWER, answer, sentences
from rag.embed import make_embedder, tokens
from rag.index import build_index

GOLDEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "evals" / "golden.jsonl"


def faithfulness(answer_text, hits, threshold=0.7):
    """Share of answer sentences that are supported by the chunks they cite.

    A sentence counts as supported when it cites at least one retrieved chunk and
    at least `threshold` of its content words appear in the cited chunk text.
    A crude, cheap proxy; an LLM-as-judge is the usual upgrade.
    """
    if answer_text == NO_ANSWER:
        return 1.0
    by_id = {c.id: c.text for c, _ in hits}
    sents = sentences(answer_text)
    supported = 0
    for s in sents:
        cited = re.findall(r"\[([\w#]+)\]", s)
        source = " ".join(by_id.get(c, "") for c in cited)
        words = set(tokens(re.sub(r"\[[\w#]+\]", "", s)))
        if cited and source and words and len(words & set(tokens(source))) / len(words) >= threshold:
            supported += 1
    return supported / len(sents) if sents else 0.0


def run(k=3):
    embedder = make_embedder()
    store = build_index(embedder)
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in GOLDEN.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    hits_at_k, facts_ok, faith, leaks, answerable = 0, 0, [], 0, 0
    print(f"{'id':<4} {'recall':<6} {'fact':<5} {'faith':<5} question")
    for row in rows:
        result = answer(row["question"], store, embedder, row["groups"], k)
        docs = [c.doc_id for c, _ in result["hits"]]
        f = faithfulness(result["answer"], result["hits"])
        faith.append(f)
        if row["expected_doc"]:
            answerable += 1
            hit = row["expected_doc"] in docs
            fact = row["fact"].lower() in result["answer"].lower()
            hits_at_k += hit
            facts_ok += fact
            print(f"{row['id']:<4} {'yes' if hit else 'NO':<6} {'yes' if fact else 'NO':<5} {f:<5.2f} {row['question']}")
        else:
            leaked = row["forbidden_doc"] in docs
            leaks += leaked
            print(f"{row['id']:<4} {'-':<6} {'-':<5} {f:<5.2f} {row['question']}  (ACL check: {'LEAK' if leaked else 'ok'})")
    summary = {
        f"recall@{k}": round(hits_at_k / answerable, 3),
        "fact_accuracy": round(facts_ok / answerable, 3),
        "faithfulness": round(sum(faith) / len(faith), 3),
        "acl_leaks": leaks,
        "questions": len(rows),
    }
    print("\n" + json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    return summary


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=3)
    s = run(parser.parse_args().k)
    gates_ok = list(s.values())[0] >= 0.8 and s["faithfulness"] >= 0.8 and s["acl_leaks"] == 0
    sys.exit(0 if gates_ok else 1)

steps.title: Test the pipeline
steps.body: Tests cover document loading, chunk sizes and ids, deterministic embeddings, citations, the ACL filter for both a regular and an HR user, the faithfulness check on a supported and an invented sentence, and the full golden set against the gates.
steps.code:
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
os.environ["LLM_MODE"] = "fake"
os.environ["EMBED_MODE"] = "hash"

from eval import faithfulness, run  # noqa: E402
from rag.answer import NO_ANSWER, answer  # noqa: E402
from rag.embed import HashingEmbedder  # noqa: E402
from rag.index import build_index, chunk_doc, load_docs  # noqa: E402


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def setup():
    emb = HashingEmbedder()
    return build_index(emb), emb


def test_ten_docs_with_acls():
    docs = load_docs()
    assert len(docs) == 10
    assert {d["acl"] for d in docs} == {"all", "hr", "finance"}


def test_chunks_respect_size_and_keep_ids():
    doc = {"id": "d", "title": "T", "acl": "all", "body": "\n\n".join(["x" * 150] * 5)}
    chunks = chunk_doc(doc, max_chars=400)
    assert [c.id for c in chunks] == ["d#0", "d#1", "d#2"]
    assert all(len(c.text) <= 400 for c in chunks)


def test_hashing_embedder_is_deterministic_and_normalized():
    a, b = HashingEmbedder().embed(["remote work stipend"]), HashingEmbedder().embed(["remote work stipend"])
    assert np.allclose(a, b) and np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(a[0]), 1.0)


def test_answer_cites_top_chunk(setup):
    store, emb = setup
    out = answer("How many weeks of parental leave do primary caregivers get?", store, emb)
    assert "16 weeks" in out["answer"] and "[parental_leave#0]" in out["answer"]


def test_acl_blocks_hr_doc_for_regular_user(setup):
    store, emb = setup
    out = answer("What is the salary band for L3 engineers?", store, emb, groups=[])
    assert all(c.acl == "all" for c, _ in out["hits"])
    assert "95,000" not in out["answer"]
    assert "95,000" in answer("What is the salary band for L3 engineers?", store, emb, groups=["hr"])["answer"]


def test_faithfulness_flags_unsupported_sentence(setup):
    store, emb = setup
    hits = answer("How long must passwords be?", store, emb)["hits"]
    good = "Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and unique to each system. [security#0]"
    bad = "Passwords must be changed every week by the CEO personally. [security#0]"
    assert faithfulness(good, hits) == 1.0
    assert faithfulness(bad, hits) == 0.0
    assert faithfulness(NO_ANSWER, hits) == 1.0


def test_golden_set_meets_quality_gates():
    summary = run(k=3)
    assert summary["questions"] == 15
    assert summary["recall@3"] >= 0.8 and summary["faithfulness"] >= 0.8 and summary["acl_leaks"] == 0

project.interview: I built a small RAG system over policy documents with ACL filtering applied before ranking, chunk-level citations, abstention when retrieval is weak, and an eval script over a 15-question golden set that reports recall@k, fact accuracy, faithfulness and ACL leaks and fails CI when they drop. It runs fully offline with a hashing embedder and numpy, and swaps to sentence-transformers, pgvector and Claude via environment variables. Trade-offs I would mention: lexical embeddings are cheap and predictable but miss synonyms, a word-overlap faithfulness check is fast but crude compared with an LLM judge, and a golden set this small shows regressions but is not a statistically strong benchmark.

ideas: Measure retrieval separately from generation: if the right chunk is not retrieved, no prompt can fix the answer.
Apply permission filters before ranking so restricted text never reaches the model.
Citations with chunk ids make every answer checkable, by humans and by an automated faithfulness check.
An eval script with thresholds and an exit code turns quality into a CI gate.
traps: Filtering ACLs after retrieval, or only in the prompt, so restricted text still lands in the context.
Judging a RAG system by reading a few answers instead of measuring recall@k on a fixed golden set.
Keeping a similarity threshold after switching embedders; score scales differ between models.
qa: Your RAG bot gives a wrong answer. How do you debug it?

First check retrieval: was the correct chunk in the top k? If not, fix chunking, embeddings, query rewriting or add hybrid search. If it was retrieved but the answer is wrong, it is a generation problem: fix the prompt, citation rules or context order. Add the case to the golden set so it stays fixed.
What does recall@k measure and why is it not enough on its own?

It measures the share of questions where a relevant document appears in the top k results. It says nothing about whether the answer used that document correctly, so you also need faithfulness (is every claim supported by a cited chunk) and answer correctness, plus safety checks such as ACL leaks.
